title: India's U18 Men Fought Back to 2-2. Then Japan Scored Twice in Eight Minutes.
excerpt: The hosts beat India 4-2 in their opening Pool A match at the Asia Cup in Kakamigahara. India face South Korea on Monday with qualification still in their own hands.
body:
India equalised. Then Japan took the game away.

The Indian U18 men's hockey team lost 4-2 to hosts Japan in their opening Pool A fixture at the Asia Cup 2026 in Kakamigahara on Sunday. It was a match that India appeared to have wrestled back to level terms, only for Japan's penalty corner variations and clinical finishing to prove decisive in the third quarter.

## A Game of Momentum Swings

The opening quarter was cagey, with both sides scrapping for midfield control and neither creating a clear chance. Japan broke through first in the fifteenth minute. Captain Yoshioka Mahiro finished with a diving deflection after a well-rehearsed penalty corner variation, Watanabe Atsuhiro playing a reverse pass back to the injector to wrong-foot the Indian defence.

Five minutes into the second quarter, it was 2-0. Fujiwara Yuma collected the ball on the left flank, beat his marker with a sharp turn, and unleashed a backhand shot that arrowed into the top right corner. The goal was as good as any scored in the tournament so far — a reminder that Japan, playing in front of their home crowd, had prepared specifically for this fixture.

India responded. In the twenty-fifth minute, Ashish Tani Purti converted a penalty corner with a precise low drag-flick to cut the deficit to 2-1 going into half-time. The visitors came out with intensity in the third quarter, and in the thirty-second minute, captain Ketan Kushwaha pounced.

A penalty corner was saved by the Japanese goalkeeper, but the clearance was poor. Kushwaha, lurking at the edge of the circle, chipped the loose ball over the sprawling keeper. India were level at 2-2. The Kakamigahara crowd fell silent.

## Eight Minutes That Decided It

The equaliser lasted two minutes. Japan won a penalty corner in the thirty-fourth minute and executed another variation: Watanabe fed Yasui Kengo with a firm pass to the right of the circle, and Kengo tapped in first time. The restart had barely happened before Japan were 3-2 ahead.

India pressed for another equaliser, committing players forward. Japan punished the gaps. In the forty-second minute, Takahashi Aone received the ball in space on a transition and beat the Indian goalkeeper with a composed finish. At 4-2, the game was effectively over. India pushed in the final quarter but could not create the chances their effort deserved.

## Context for the Diaspora

While the men's team fell to the hosts, the Indian U18 women's side had a much better day in the same venue. Nousheen Naz, the fifteen-year-old who has now scored in every match, helped India beat South Korea 3-1 to go top of their pool with a perfect record.

The contrast is striking. India's women's hockey development programme has produced a generation of players who appear ready for senior competition. The men's U18 side, while competitive, were outmanoeuvred by a Japanese team whose penalty corner routines looked weeks ahead in preparation.

## What's Next

India face South Korea on Monday — June 1 at 7 PM local time in Kakamigahara (3:30 PM IST). Korea thrashed Kazakhstan 13-0 in their opener, so India will need a significant improvement in penalty corner defence to stay in contention for the semi-finals. Qualification is still in their own hands. A win against Korea would level the pool and set up a decisive final round of matches.

For NRI hockey fans, the tournament is not streamed on any Indian OTT platform, but Hockey India has been posting highlights and results on their social channels. The men's team's next match is the one that matters.
author: Diaspora Desk
